INTRODUCTION FOR TEENS
“But I Don’t Do Davening!”
(“OK, I do davening, but I don’t enjoy it!”)OK, I get that. That is actually the most common comment 
made by young people who struggle with davening. “Did you daven this morning?” “No.” “Why not?” “I dunno.” “I dunno is not an answer!” “I dunno — I just don’t DO davening.”
So we need to figure out

you don’t do davening, or even 
if you do daven, why you find it so hard and not enjoyable. You’ve heard all the
, speeches, guest speakers, Yom Iyuns, workshops, and

classes. You’ve read all the books, tried all the workbooks, workshops, methods, and surefire tricks. You’ve been offered prizes — and threatened. Yet, for some reason, you look at the siddur and freeze! Or worse — you open it, try your hardest to daven, and mess up! Then you feel even more guilty than you did before, and you’re more convinced than ever that “Hashem certainly will not answer a mess- up like me!” Now you’re even further from your goal! And you
want to daven and enjoy davening (or at least you want to
to daven and enjoy it). You see that bachur

away with his face contorted with emotion, or that girl with her siddur stuck right up to her face crying, and you wonder, “Why can’t I be like them? What’s the matter with me?”
